newsitem.title: UK: ORANGE DOUBLES INVESTMENT TO BOOST NETWORK.
newsitem.headline: ORANGE DOUBLES INVESTMENT TO BOOST NETWORK.

text.p: Orange Plc, Britain's third biggest mobile telephone company, said on Thursday it would double to 800 million pounds investments in its network, so it could introduce new services to help win new customers.

Having broken into positive EBIDTA (earnings before interest, depreciation, tax and amortisation), Orange said it was considering the launch of new services such as Internet browsing, home shopping, on-line newspapers and financial services and narrow-band television.

The company said it planned to make the investment by the end of 1999, by bringing forward 400 million stg of capital expenditure scheduled for the year 2000 and beyond. Orange will have invested more than 1.6 billion stg in its wirefree network by the next century.

"We are confident that the impact of superior coverage, that extends customer excpectations, will grow the market faster, increase our market share, widen wirefree usage, increase chargeable usage and average customer revenues and acheive greater profitability," said managing director Hans Snook in the results statement.

Orange's pre-tax loss in the half year narrowed by 41 percent to 73.5 million stg, beating most analyst expectations. Revenues per subscriber rose nine percent to 40.16 stg per month and were running at 500 stg per year, up 13 percent, from 1996 levels, the group said.
